name: Convection
blurb: A layer of gas whose temperature falls upward faster than the adiabat, between walls in a uniform field: warm gas from below rises, cool gas from above sinks, and two seeded pairs of cells grow into convection at about Mach 0.1 within a few tens of time units, mixing the two halves (the colour). The layer is built in the grid's own hydrostatic balance, stored as its difference from the layer at rest (Reference state: Column), and its density reconstructed along the adiabat (Solver), which keeps a layer at the adiabat from convecting on its own. The flow's speed grows as the square root of the superadiabatic excess: Mach 0.3 at 0.1, 0.02 to 0.03 at 1e-3, 0.0075 at 1e-4. Below about 1e-4 on 128 cells the scheme's own error in the layer's buoyancy sets the flow instead: deep in a star, where the excess is 1e-6 or less, is out of reach so far.

featured.label: Superadiabatic excess
featured.tip: How much steeper than the adiabat the layer is (dln T / dln p less (gamma - 1) / gamma). The cells turn at about Mach 0.3 at 0.1, 0.1 at 0.01, 0.025 at 1e-3, 0.0075 at 1e-4: as its square root, and the steps they take grow in proportion. Below about 1e-4 on 128 cells (less on finer grids) the scheme's own error in the buoyancy is larger than the excess, and the flow is the grid's. Changing it starts the run again
